title: How a Wi-Fi Router Works in 60 Seconds 📶🌐 #shorts
description:
A Wi-Fi router turns internet data into radio waves. Data from the modem is split into small addressed packets, the antennas send them as radio waves at 2.4 or 5 gigahertz, and the router keeps track of every device so each packet reaches the right one. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#wifi #router #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Your *Wi-Fi* signal is a radio wave that wiggles *2.4 billion* times every second.

steps.label: Cable in
steps.text: The internet arrives through a cable from the *modem* into the *router*.

steps.label: Packets
steps.text: All data is chopped into small *packets*, each one labeled with an *address*.

steps.label: Radio
steps.text: The antennas send those packets out as *radio waves*, at *2.4* or *5* gigahertz.

steps.label: Devices
steps.text: Your phone's antenna *catches* them, and sends its own replies back the *same way*.

steps.label: Traffic cop
steps.text: The router gives every device a *local address* and sends each packet to the *right one*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Cable, packets, *radio*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
